headline: Free AI training for youth in 64 districts, daily allowance of BDT 200
summary: The Directorate of Youth Development is offering a 50-day fundamental AI training program across Bangladesh. Participants will receive a daily allowance and meals, enhancing their IT skills for future opportunities.
details: The Directorate of Youth Development has launched an initiative to provide fundamental Artificial Intelligence (AI) training to young individuals across all 64 districts of Bangladesh. This program aims to enhance IT skills among the youth, preparing them for the evolving technological landscape.

Part of the 'Skill Development of IT-Knowledgeable Youth through Artificial Intelligence Technology' project, this second batch of training will run for 50 days, from October 1 to November 30. It will comprise 50 classes, totaling 300 hours of instruction.
Eligible candidates must be between 18 and 35 years old, have at least an HSC or equivalent qualification, and possess basic computer and IT knowledge. There are no training fees for this course.

Interested applicants can apply online until 11:59 PM on September 23. A written examination is scheduled for September 26, followed by an oral examination on September 27 for selected candidates. The final list of selected participants will be published on September 29, with notifications sent via SMS.

During the training period, participants will receive a daily travel allowance of BDT 200, along with provided meals. Upon successful completion of the program, all participants will be awarded a certificate.

headline: Bangladesh Bank launches 'Uddyog' program for youth, offering BDT 20 lakh aid
summary: Bangladesh Bank's new 'Uddyog' program offers up to BDT 20 lakh to young entrepreneurs, combining interest-free loans and grants to combat unemployment and foster new businesses.
details: Bangladesh Bank's new 'Uddyog' program aims to tackle severe unemployment and create alternative employment opportunities. The formal application process for this initiative, designed to turn job-seekers into entrepreneurs, began on Wednesday, September 16, 2026. This central bank step seeks to identify promising young individuals at the upazila level and provide them with business capital.
In its initial phase, the program will operate in 64 upazilas across eight districts in eight divisions: Manikganj, Feni, Naogaon, Jhenaidah, Bhola, Habiganj, Rangpur, and Netrokona.

Selected candidates can receive up to BDT 20 lakh for new or existing businesses. A key feature of this funding is the inclusion of both loans and grants. Fifty percent of the total assistance, up to BDT 10 lakh, will be provided as a bank loan, with the remaining 50 percent, up to BDT 10 lakh, given as a one-time grant.

Bangladesh Bank confirms that entrepreneurs will not need to provide any collateral for this funding. However, ensuring the proper use of the funds provided by the bank is mandatory. Failure to repay loan installments on time or using the funds for other purposes will result in the cancellation of the grant benefit, converting the grant amount into a loan recoverable as government dues.

Applicants must meet specific conditions under national law to qualify. Candidates must be under 28 years old on the application deadline, be a permanent resident of the relevant upazila, and possess a viable business idea or plan.

Individuals who have previously taken loans from any bank or financial institution, loan defaulters, or employees of government, semi-government, and autonomous institutions are ineligible. Any incorrect or false information in the application will lead to direct cancellation.

Young people in sectors like agro-based industries, food processing, handicrafts, fisheries, livestock, tourism, light engineering, and renewable energy will benefit. Additionally, tech-dependent startups, including e-commerce, fintech, edtech, agritech, and healthtech, along with any other income-generating legal ventures, will be financed.

Applications can be downloaded from Bangladesh Bank's official website, the SME portal, and the websites of all scheduled banks. Completed forms, along with a national ID, citizenship certificate, photo, and educational/training certificates (if applicable), should be submitted to any scheduled bank branch in the applicant's area.
